chapter: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
title: Candy Johnson's search for Ben Webster
summary: On the tour Candy Johnson tracked down Ben Webster in Denmark with Johnny Simmons's help, spent four days with him, and Webster died two weeks later.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, you know, it's a funny thing, isn't it, that -- I mean this guy has done these tours, and everybody else has sort of taken the same old names back year after year, same people go year after year, and he keeps taking
all kinds of people like that. I mean they'd never heard of Candy Johnson until he took him.

Yeah, well, Candy'd been around. He used to be with the old Andy Kirk band. He was with Bill Doggett after the Scotty (inaudible) left. He's been around for a while, but he's mainly stationed in Toledo. He teaches school there, and his wife does too, in the same school. So this year he just -- they called him on the short notice, and he paid his own way over there, and they had to reimburse him.

And he had his wife, and he was determined to find Ben Webster. For some reason or another he had to see Ben. But he could not find out where Ben was or where he went. So we got to Zurich, Switzerland, and he saw Johnny Simmons. Johnny Simmons is a writer.

Knew everybody. Knew their whereabouts, and he told him where Ben Webster was, in Denmark. Gave him his phone number and everything. And he called him from Zurich, from Zurich. He said, 'I just want to know if you were there.' Now (inaudible) he just -- all he want to do, because he loved Ben Webster. He put his wife on a plane to go back to the States, and he went up there and stayed four days.
Now (inaudible) he wrote a letter saying about his situation. He enjoyed Dexter Gordon coming to town. They had

a party at Dexter's house, and they jammed for four days together at different clubs, and two weeks later Ben's dead, two weeks later. And there's -- so that's why I say, he must have had a premonition because he was determined. He was asking everybody about Ben Webster, Ben -- he said, 'I've got to see him while I'm on this trip, while I'm over here.' And good thing he did see him, because if he'd left and didn't see him, he never would have seen him anymore anyway.
